newsitem.title: UK: Prompt IPE gas oil jumps, Sep/Oct spread balloons.
newsitem.headline: Prompt IPE gas oil jumps, Sep/Oct spread balloons.

text.p: Prompt IPE gas oil rallied sharply Thursday, extending its premium over outer months amid short-covering ahead of next week's expiry and October's change to European diesel specifications, dealers said.
"The spread has blown out completely. There's some good front month buying by a couple of brokers," said one.
Sept gas oil, which expires on September 12, traded up $5.00 at $212.50 a tonne by 1548 GMT. Oct was at $203.50, up $1.25.
"Someone got caught short up front. It's the kind of thing we're going to have to expect ahead of expiry," said a broker.

The European gas oil pool, currently 0.2 percent sulphur for both heating oil and diesel, will be split 60:40 into 0.2 percent for heating oil and 0.05 percent for diesel from October 1. The IPE contract will continue to specify only 0.2 percent.
Dealers said planned maintenance at refineries in the Rotterdam area may have left two oil majors short of prompt barrels.
IPE Brent crude was helped to session highs in midafternoon trade by the strong gas oil performance and gains on NYMEX crude, dealers said.
Oct Brent was down three cents at $22.08 by 1600 GMT.
Dealers said Hurricane Fran, expected to make landfall along the south Carolina Coast this evening, could be helping to lift U.S. market sentiment.
Amoco Corp's Yorktown refinery was operating normally and had not suspended oil product shipments, a company spokesman said.
Operations at other major refineries in the area were also unaffected although they continued to track the storm closely.
